resources.string: While a chosen app is open, banners are replaced by a scrolling line, and the alerts stay in the shade.
Turns on by itself while a chosen app is in front. Ordinary alerts go silent and stay in the shade. Calls, alarms, and media still come through.
The switch stays off until notification access, Do Not Disturb access, and display over other apps are all granted.
Reads the title and text for the strip. When the notification access screen shows toggles, leave alerting, silent, and conversations on for Ribbon Notifs.
Lets Ribbon Notifs hide banners for ordinary alerts. Those alerts stay in the shade, without sound or vibration.
Draws the thin strip. The strip does not take taps, so the app underneath still receives every touch.
Sees which app is in front so Ribbon Notifs can turn on by itself. Without this, nothing arms automatically.
These are system settings, not one-time permission dialogs. Android can ask for them again after Ribbon Notifs sits unused for a long time.
Do Not Disturb access is off, so banners will keep appearing. The strip can still show alerts the listener sees.
That system screen is not available on this phone.
Allow display over other apps before previewing the strip.
No apps chosen yet. Search to add one. Tap a chosen app to remove it.
Ribbon Notifs: This is a preview ribbon notification. Adjust the size, scrolling speed and background to preview. This is what it looks like across the screen.
If silence stays on after leaving a chosen app, this turns the quiet rule off.
While a chosen app is in front, ordinary alerts go silent and scroll by as a ribbon.

Records why each alert was shown or skipped. Message text is not included.

Ribbon Notifs turns on while a selected app is open. Notifications stay in the shade.
Ordinary alerts go silent for that time. Calls, alarms, and media still come through. Turn it off from Ribbon Notifs, or leave the selected app.
